newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea oil/NGL output excluding UK fell in February.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea oil/NGL output excluding UK fell in February.

text.p: Oil/NGL production from the North Sea (excluding UK) in February averaged an estimated 6.17 million barrels per day (bpd), down 50,000 bpd on the average produced in January, analysts Wood Mackenzie said on Thursday.
Norwegian oil/NGL production was little changed with output up 10,000 bpd at 3.4 million bpd, Wood Mackenzie said in a monthly report.

It added that bad weather in February disrupted some loadings and led to falls in output from some platforms. Shutdown on Gullfaks resulted in a fall of around 45,000 bpd from Gullfaks itself, and a decrease of around 13,000 bpd from Tordis. Production was also halted on Saga's Snorre platform, resulting in a fall in output of around 40,000 bpd.

Danish production fell slightly again in February to average around 217,000 bpd, a fall of around five percent from January, Wood Mackenzie said. This was due largely to a drop of around 3,000 bpd in output from Gorm and 8,000 bpd from Svend.
Dutch production fell by seven percent or around 2,500 bpd in February due to small decreases in output from most fields.
